questions: UBER has spent the entire day pinned within a few cents of $69.6 with zero fresh news, while SPY quietly rallied over 0.5% intraday -- does UBER's failure to participate in a broad-market up day tell you anything about how the market is treating the stock differently from the index, or is this just noise?

The DCF/consensus gap (now ~73%/50%) has persisted for over a month without closing -- at what point does that persistence become information that the market has a better read on litigation/AV-competition risk than the model, rather than a mispricing worth holding through?

Elsewhere on the watchlist today AVAV extended its slide to a ~46% discount to consensus with no fresh catalyst, and NVO continued its post-Capital-Markets-Day slide to a fresh multi-week low -- if you're comfortable holding UBER through a similarly wide, catalyst-less gap, why hasn't that same logic been applied to sizing into either of those names instead of leaving cash idle?

This position is still ~71% of NAV with no decision made today to hold it there -- if you were assembling this portfolio from cash right now, would you still put 71% of it into UBER, or does the honest answer point to a rebalancing decision that keeps getting deferred?
